chunks: Ibn Maskān narrated from Yazīd ibn Khalīfah, who said:

There was a basket beside my house in which there were two eggs from the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary. My servant went and overturned the basket, not knowing that there were two eggs in it, and he broke them. So I went out and met ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan, and I mentioned that to him. He said: 'Give in charity two handfuls of flour.' He said: Then afterward I met Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and informed him, so he عليه السلام said to me: 'He is liable for the price of two birds, with which he feeds the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary.' Then I met ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥasan and informed him, so he said: 'He has spoken the truth; act upon it, for he took it from his forefathers عليهم السلام.'

key_terms.آبَائِهِ: his forefathers, referring to the transmitted authority of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.بَيْضَتَانِ: two eggs that were broken and became the subject of compensation
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ: give in charity as a proposed form of expiation or compensation
key_terms.ثَمَنُ طَيْرَيْنِ: the monetary value of two birds owed as compensation
key_terms.حَمَامِ ٱلْحَرَمِ: the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary whose sanctity entails legal protection
key_terms.يُطْعِمُ: he feeds, meaning the compensation is spent in feeding the Sanctuary’s pigeons

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone breaks the eggs of the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding damage done to the eggs of the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that compensation is the value of two birds, to be used to feed the pigeons of the Sanctuary, and this ruling is affirmed as inherited from the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
